comments.author: @chamindaabeykoon7617
comments.text:
Sri Lanka was not subjected to comprehensive territorial conquest by the Portuguese, Dutch, or British. Although these European powers employed sustained military force to establish and maintain dominion over the island’s littoral regions, their authority did not extend to the interior polities, most notably the Kingdom of Kandy, which preserved its sovereignty through diplomatic maneuvering, strategic geography, and periodic military resistance.

The transfer of sovereignty over the entire island to the British Crown occurred only in 1815, pursuant to the Kandyan Convention, a formal diplomatic instrument negotiated with the Kandyan aristocracy. This political transition was effected through legal and administrative mechanisms rather than through the culmination of a successful military campaign. As such, the unification of the island under British rule represents a constitutional and diplomatic act, rather than a conventional act of conquest.

comments.text:
4:05
This is entirely INCORRECT. Sinahala population DID NOT migrate from India in fifth the century. 
People have been migrating from India to Sri Lanka for thousands of years. The island has been inhabited by local "Hela" people's civilisation and many indigenous peoples fir thousands of years before fifth century.
The real history of human habitation in Sri Lanka goes back to some seventy thousand years, abd perhaps even far far back if we can find empirical archeological evidence to support that high probability.

replies.author: @wickramavee4365
replies.text:
​@BestTravelDocumentary4k

As far as I know, the "Balangoda man" archeological evidence and the evidence from the "Fa Hien" cave are among the oldest. Balangoda man is the oldest AMH(Anatomically Modern Human) evidence that has been found in Asia, so far. 
Wikipedia page of "Balangoda man" is a good read for your information. 

No argument that all the ancient inhabitants in Sri Lanka came from Indian mainland, because that is the logical geographical route. 

The origin of modern day Sinhala culture is more complicated. The old "Hela" culture and the people were the beginning of the modern day Sinhala people. No argument about the cultural influence of north and south Indian cultures throughout the last two millenia or so and as you notice the cultural similarities between Indians and Sri Lankans, but the influence doesn't mean an Indian cultural origin.
